### The final answer is: $\boxed{50}$

**Derivation.**  
Each photo contributes a distinct middle person (condition 2), giving at least 25 distinct people. The right-hand person is the daughter of that middle; if two different middles shared the same daughter, those two middles would have a child in common, violating condition 3. Hence the 25 daughters are all distinct and different from the middles, giving a lower bound of $25+25=50$.

To see that 50 suffices, take one couple with 25 sons (all full brothers of one another). Let the 25 middles be these 25 sons, and give each son a distinct daughter (the mothers need not appear in the album). In photo $i$, put middle = son $i$, left = son $i+1$ (indices modulo 25), and right = son $i$’s daughter. Every left is a full brother of the corresponding middle, every middle is distinct, and no two people in the album share a child. Thus exactly 50 distinct people appear, and the minimum is $50$.
